message.content:
Sure! To cast a “Malicious” verdict for the IP `22.242.75.136` on VirusTotal, you’ll send a POST request to the **/ip_addresses/{resource}/votes** endpoint (replace `{resource}` with the IP).  
Below is a quick reference – pick whichever method works best for you:

---

### 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"

IP_ADDRESS="22.242.75.136"
VOTE_JSON='{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}'

curl -X POST \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/${IP_ADDRESS}/votes \
     -H "x-apikey: ${API_KEY}" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data "${VOTE_JSON}"
```

> Replace `"YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"` with the value stored under *key_four*.

---

### 2️⃣ Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests
import json

api_key   = "YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"
ip_address= "22.242.75.136"
url       = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_address}/votes"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": api_key,
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

payload = {
    "type": "vote",
    "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious" }
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
print(response.status_code)          # Expect 200 OK / 201 Created
print(json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2))
```

Again, swap out `"YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"` for whatever token lives behind *key_four*.  

---

#### Quick checklist before sending:
| ✅ Item |
|--------|
| You’re targeting the correct resource URL (`https://.../ip_addresses/<IP>/votes`). |
| Your payload matches the required schema (`{ type: "vote", attributes: { verdict: "<value>" }}`). |
| Verdict values accepted: `"benign"`, `"suspicious"`, `"harmless"`, `"undetermined"`, `"malicious"`. |
| Include the proper authentication header (`x-apikey`) with your API key. |

That’s all—once you hit the endpoint successfully, VirusTotal will register your “Malicious” vote for that IP. Happy scanning!
